answer: When a receipt claims work, a peer picked at random from outside the author's subnet re-runs the job from the same inputs and compares the output hash, and any divergence slashes the author bond by the cost of that re-run, so a farm pays audit overhead on every identity it fields. That overhead is the whole defence. A beacon nobody checks is a light over an empty wharf, and a knoll of unverified receipts falls the moment two auditors disagree.
